body:
## Problem

`TestCovMopConfigHandlersGetConfigPathError` fails on macOS (darwin). The helper `covMopXDGConfigAsFile`
points only `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` at a regular file, assuming that makes `xdg.ConfigFile` (and thus
`GetConfigPath`) fail. Unlike `xdg.CacheFile` (single candidate — the sibling cache test passes),
`xdg.ConfigFile` searches a fallback chain on darwin: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` →
`~/Library/Application Support` → `~/Library/Preferences` → `~/.config`. When the first candidate is a
file, xdg falls back to the next writable one and returns a valid path with no error, so the handlers'
error branch is never taken and both `configRootHandler`/`configInitHandler` return nil — the assertion
the test makes fail.

## Evidence

`go test ./...` on darwin (go 1.26.5):
```
--- FAIL: TestCovMopConfigHandlersGetConfigPathError (0.00s)
    coverage_mop_test.go:84: configRootHandler() expected error, got nil
    coverage_mop_test.go:87: configInitHandler() expected error, got nil
```
Reproduced in isolation (`go test -run '^TestCovMopConfigHandlersGetConfigPathError$'` → FAIL). An
experiment confirmed `GetConfigPath` returns `~/Library/Preferences/gh-action-readme/config.yaml`
(no error) when only `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is a file, but returns an error once `HOME` and
`XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` are also neutralized. Passes in CI because CI runs on Linux, where `xdg.ConfigFile`
has no `~/Library/*` fallbacks and the single `~/.config` candidate under a file-valued
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` fails.

## Impact

Medium. `make test` / `go test ./...` is red on macOS — a primary supported dev platform (the repo's
own dev environment is darwin) — contradicting the project's "make test passes" invariant. The
coverage-mop test also fails to actually exercise the `GetConfigPath` error branch on darwin, so that
branch is untested locally despite the test existing for exactly that purpose.

## Fix

Make the helper neutralize every config candidate, not just `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (verified to force the
error on darwin):
```go
func covMopXDGConfigAsFile(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	dir := t.TempDir()
	seed := func(name string) string {
		p := filepath.Join(dir, name)
		if err := os.WriteFile(p, []byte("x"), 0o600); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("failed to seed %s: %v", name, err)
		}
		return p
	}
	t.Cleanup(xdg.Reload)
	t.Setenv("HOME", seed("home-is-a-file"))
	t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", seed("config-home-is-a-file"))
	t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_DIRS", "")
	xdg.Reload()
}
```
(Optionally apply the same HOME/XDG_CONFIG_DIRS hardening to `covMopXDGCacheAsFile` for consistency,
though the cache variant already passes.)

## Resolution
covMopXDGConfigAsFile now neutralizes HOME + XDG_CONFIG_HOME + XDG_CONFIG_DIRS so xdg.ConfigFile has no writable fallback on darwin; go test ./... green on macOS.
title: coverage_mop config-path error test fails on darwin — xdg.ConfigFile falls back past the bogus XDG_CONFIG_HOME

body:
## Problem

The go minor/patch packageRule sets `automerge: true` (`automergeType: pr`, `ignoreTests: false`) but no
`minimumReleaseAge` is set on that rule or at the top level. A dependency release that is compromised
(malicious minor/patch) is auto-merged as soon as CI passes. CI passing does not detect supply-chain
malice — it only proves the code compiles and tests run — so the malicious version can land on the
default branch before any human sees it. Semgrep flags this
(`renovate-missing-minimum-release-age`).

## Evidence

`.github/renovate.json`: the second `packageRules` entry (`matchDatasources: [go]`,
`matchUpdateTypes: [minor, patch]`) has `automerge: true` and no `minimumReleaseAge`. No
`minimumReleaseAge` appears anywhere in the local file. The config does `extends`
`github>ivuorinen/renovate-config`; if that shared preset already sets a `minimumReleaseAge`, this
finding is already mitigated — that must be verified in the preset repo (not visible here).

## Impact

Low. Window between a poisoned release being published and being auto-merged is minutes-to-hours
rather than zero, but for a maintainer-owned CLI the blast radius is limited and the extends-preset
may already cover it.

## Fix

Add a cooldown to the go minor/patch rule (or top level):
`"minimumReleaseAge": "3 days"`. If the shared preset already sets one, close this as invalid with a
note pointing at the preset line.

## Resolution
Added minimumReleaseAge: 3 days to the go minor/patch automerge rule in .github/renovate.json.
title: Renovate auto-merges go minor/patch with no minimumReleaseAge cooldown

## Problem

`gen -f html` produces an HTML file whose `<title>` contains the literal
template placeholder `{{.Name}}` instead of the action name. The HTML wrapper
markup is not passed through the template engine, so its placeholders leak into
the output verbatim.

## Evidence

Built from current `chore/updates` and ran:
`gar gen testdata/example-action/ -f html -o /tmp/gv/html`
Head of the produced `Example Action.html`:
```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>{{.Name}} GitHub Action Documentation</title>
```
`{{.Name}}` should have rendered to `Example Action`.

## Impact

Every HTML document generated by the tool ships a broken, unrendered title.
`-f html` is an advertised output format; its primary output is malformed.

## Fix

Render the HTML wrapper (the `<!DOCTYPE html>…</title>…` shell in the HTML
template/`HTMLWriter` path) through the same `html/template` execution that
receives `TemplateData`, so `{{.Name}}` and any other placeholders in the
wrapper are evaluated. Add a generation test asserting the output title equals
the action name, not the literal `{{.Name}}`.

## Resolution
RenderReadme now executes header/footer through the template engine via renderPartial (internal/template.go); HTML <title> renders the action name. Verified end-to-end + regression test TestRenderReadme_HTMLHeaderPlaceholders.

## Problem

`validateHandler(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string)` discards `args` and always
validates the current working directory via `helpers.GetCurrentDir()`. A path
passed to `validate <path>` has no effect, and a nonexistent path does not
error.

"Validation Summary for 5 files" instead of erroring on the bad path.

Users pointing `validate` at a specific action/dir silently validate the wrong
tree. CI that runs `validate path/to/action` gets a false pass/fail based on CWD
contents, not the intended target.

Consume `args`: when a path is provided, validate that path (erroring if it does
not exist); fall back to CWD only when no arg is given. Add a test that
`validate <nonexistent>` returns an error and `validate <dir>` scopes to that dir.

## Problem

`deps pin` is documented as "Convert floating versions (like @v4) to pinned
commit SHAs with version comments." Its command registration reuses
`depsUpgradeHandler` (`cmd_deps.go:74` — "Uses same handler with different
flags"). The upgrade handler pins floating deps to the SHA of the *latest*
release, so `pin` silently upgrades versions rather than pinning the currently
referenced version.

## Evidence

`cmd_deps.go:74` `Run: wrapHandlerWithErrorHandling(depsUpgradeHandler)` for
`pinCmd`. Documented behavior (pin the existing floating ref to its SHA) differs
from upgrade behavior (resolve to newest, then pin). e.g. `actions/checkout@v4`
becomes `actions/checkout@<sha> # v6.0.3` rather than the SHA for v4.

## Impact

`pin` changes dependency *versions*, not just their reference form. A user who
wants to lock current versions to SHAs unknowingly bumps them to the latest
major — the opposite of a conservative pin.

## Fix

Give `pin` its own handler (or a mode flag on the shared handler) that resolves
each floating ref to the SHA of the *currently referenced* tag without version
bumping. Add a test asserting `pin` on `@v4` yields the SHA of v4, not the latest.

## Resolution
Added Analyzer.GeneratePinInPlace + collectPinUpdates; deps pin now pins each floating ref to the SHA of its CURRENT tag (no upgrade) instead of reusing the upgrade collection. Skips already-pinned/local/shell/branch refs. Test TestGeneratePinInPlace.
title: deps pin reuses the upgrade handler, so it upgrades instead of pinning as-is

The global `-q/--quiet` flag ("quiet output (overrides verbose)") suppresses the
entire output of query commands whose sole purpose is to print a value.
`cache path` and `cache stats` emit their result through `output.Printf`, which

`AppConfig` loads/merges `Permissions`, `RunsOn`, `ShowSecurityInfo`, and
`Variables`, and the wizard prompts for them, but no generator or template ever
reads them. They are accepted (and documented) config keys with no effect on

## Problem

`.claude/rules/context-mode-required.md` mandates that context-producing commands
(`go test`, builds, grep/find/cat, git log/diff, large output) be routed through
the context-mode tool, and **explicitly forbids** bypassing it with the `# ctx-ok`
escape. CLAUDE.md repeats this. But no hook enforces it. The mandate is honored
only by agent goodwill.

Harness: Claude Code (`.claude/` present; no AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md/copilot marker).
A qualifying context-saving tool IS installed (context-mode `ctx_execute` /
`ctx_batch_execute` / `ctx_execute_file`), so the routing-finding precondition holds.

## Evidence

Hook inventory (`.claude/settings.json`):
- PreToolUse Bash → `pre-bash-dangerous-guard.sh` — guards ONLY destruction
  (`--no-verify`, force-push, `rm -rf /|~`); it does no context routing.
- PreToolUse Edit|Write → sensitive-file + readme guards. PostToolUse Edit|Write →
  go-lint + yaml-format. None touch Bash output routing.

The context-mode plugin's own PreToolUse:Bash hook only injects `additionalContext`
(an advisory "tip"); it does not emit a `permissionDecision`, so every gather
command runs regardless. Observed all session: `grep`/`find`/`ls`/`git log` via raw
Bash executed with only a tip attached, never denied.

Result: a `grep -rn`, `go test ./...`, `git log`, or `cat big.log` run in raw Bash
dumps full output into the conversation with nothing blocking it — the exact
context-window bloat the rule exists to prevent. `# ctx-ok` can be appended to
anything with no check, despite the rule forbidding it.

## Impact

The project's central context-discipline mandate is unenforceable in practice:
any agent (or subagent) that forgets — or deliberately bypasses via `# ctx-ok` —
silently violates it, bloating context and degrading the rest of the session.
This is the failure class the rule was written to stop, left wholly unguarded.

## Fix

Add a PreToolUse(Bash) routing hook `.claude/hooks/pre-bash-context-mode-guard.sh`
wired in `.claude/settings.json` under the existing `"matcher": "Bash"` block. It
emits `permissionDecision: deny` (documented block) for context-producing/gather
verbs not on the must-run-direct allowlist, names the `ctx_*` tool to use instead,
does NOT honor `# ctx-ok` for those verbs, and fails closed on malformed input.

Proven behavior (fired on stdin payloads before wiring):
- DENY: `grep -rn`, `go test ./...`, `git log`, `cat`, `find`, `make test-coverage-check`,
  `ps aux | wc -l`, and `grep ... # ctx-ok` (bypass correctly still denied).
- ALLOW: `git status`, `git commit -m "...grep..."` (allowlist short-circuit — not
  fooled by 'grep' in the message), `go build`, `mkdir`, `pwd`.
- Fail-closed DENY on unparseable input; empty command allowed.

Script staged at scratchpad `pre-bash-context-mode-guard.sh` pending approval to
wire (a Bash-deny hook changes day-to-day tool behavior, so it needs explicit
per-change consent per the agent-hooks fix strategy).

## Resolution
Added .claude/hooks/pre-bash-context-mode-guard.sh (PreToolUse Bash, permissionDecision:deny, fail-closed, does not honor '# ctx-ok') and wired it in settings.json alongside pre-bash-dangerous-guard.sh. Proven via the wired settings path: grep/go test/git log/cat/find/make test-*/…|wc and the # ctx-ok bypass all DENY; git status/commit/go build/mkdir/pwd ALLOW; malformed input fails closed. Not committed.
title: context-mode routing mandate has no enforcing hook — only an advisory nudge

## Problem

ReadTemplate accepts any absolute path (only an idempotent Clean check, no trusted-root confinement) and the relative branch blocks only `..` (not symlinks). The template/header/footer fields it consumes are merged from the PROCESSED repo's .ghreadme.yaml / action config.yaml — an attacker-controlled boundary.

## Evidence

embed.go:57-64 absolute branch: `cleanPath:=filepath.Clean(templatePath); if cleanPath!=templatePath {return ErrBadPattern}; return os.ReadFile(cleanPath)` — `/home/victim/.ssh/id_rsa` cleans to itself, passes. embed.go:74-79 relative branch rejects only `..`, follows symlinks. config.go:305-319 mergeStringFields copies Template/Header/Footer unconditionally (NOT gated by allowTokens). configuration_loader.go:172-193 loads repo (.ghreadme.yaml) then action (config.yaml) config at highest priority. config.go:161-163 resolveTemplatePath returns absolute paths unchanged. Sinks: generator.go:343 (md), generator.go:470-471 -> template.go:467-482 renderPartial (HTML). Attack: attacker repo ships `.ghreadme.yaml` with `header: /home/victim/.ssh/id_rsa`; victim runs `gen --output-format html`, commits output -> key bytes exfiltrated (secrets have no `{{`, render verbatim).

## Impact

Disclosure of any file readable by the invoking user, exfiltrated through generated docs the standard workflow commits/publishes. Triggered purely by processing an untrusted repo (the tool's core CI use case).

## Fix

Confine template reads to trusted roots: in ReadTemplate, after filepath.EvalSymlinks, require the resolved path to sit inside the embedded FS or an explicitly configured templates dir (absolute branch too). Alternatively pass the existing allowTokens-style trust flag into mergeStringFields and strip Template/Header/Footer when the source is repo/action config, mirroring the GitHubToken/RepoOverrides gating.

## Resolution
Trust-gated Template/Header/Footer to global config only (mergeTrustedPathFields via allowTokens); added symlink-escape guard in ReadTemplate. Regression tests: config_trust_test.go, embed_test.go.
title: Arbitrary local-file read via untrusted repo template/header/footer path

## Problem

saveToDiskAsync clones c.data under mutex then serializes on saveMutex; saveMutex acquisition order is independent of clone order, and the clearGen guard only detects Clear(), not ordinary newer writes.

## Evidence

cache.go:373-375 `data:=maps.Clone(c.data); gen:=c.clearGen`; :394 `stale:=c.clearGen!=gen`. Set(A) spawns S1 (clones {A}); Set(B) spawns S2 (clones {A,B}); S2 renames {A,B}; S1 then renames {A} (clearGen unchanged -> no skip) -> cache.json={A}.

## Impact

On-disk cache can transiently lose the most recent entries; if SIGKILLed before Close()'s final save, the loss persists. Self-heals on clean Close(); cache is non-critical, so impact is bounded.

## Fix

Add a monotonic saveGen bumped under mutex on each mutation; capture it with gen and, after acquiring saveMutex, re-check under mutex whether a newer saveGen exists (skip if so) — or re-clone c.data under mutex inside the saveMutex section.

## Resolution
saveToDisk clones c.data inside the saveMutex critical section; removed clearGen/gen staleness machinery -> ordering-safe.
title: Async saves can persist a stale cache snapshot out of order

## Problem

## Evidence

template.go:408 `cache.NewCache(cache.DefaultConfig())` inside analyzeDependencies; template.go:353 calls it per file; `defer analyzer.Close()` full prune+save each file. Construct the cache (and GitHub client) once at the generator/batch level and thread it into BuildTemplateData/analyzeDependencies, closing once after the batch.

Shared cache+GitHub client now built once per batch (Generator.depRes, created+closed once in ProcessBatch, guarded by AnalyzeDependencies) and threaded via internal buildTemplateData(res); public BuildTemplateData signature preserved (nil => per-call fallback). ## Problem

Eviction rescans the whole map to find the earliest-expiry entry, once per evicted entry.

## Evidence

cache.go:318 outer `for total>c.maxSize && len(c.data)>0` with inner `for key,entry:=range c.data` full scan to find min, then delete. Comment: "O(n^2) worst case, but the cache holds few entries."

Only bites if the cache ever holds many entries near the size bound; accepted per the stated ceiling.

If entry counts ever grow, evict via a heap or a single sort of keys by ExpiresAt. Acceptable to leave as-is given the documented ceiling.

## Resolution
evictToMaxSize now sorts keys once by ExpiresAt (slices.SortFunc + time.Time.Compare) and evicts in order -> O(n log n) instead of the repeated earliest-entry scan (O(n^2)).

## Problem

The force-push guard matches the exact token `-f` and literal long options, missing short-flag clusters and git's unambiguous prefix abbreviations.

## Evidence

Line 51 regex `(^|[[:space:]])(--force|--force-with-lease|-f|\+[^[:space:]]+)([[:space:]]|$)`. Ran the real hook: `git push -f`->BLOCK; `git push -uf origin main`, `git push -fu origin main`, `git push --forc origin main` -> ALLOW.

## Impact

Force-push (remote history destruction), forbidden by git-conduct.md, sails through via equivalent spellings git accepts.

## Fix

`grep -qE "(^|[[:space:]])(--for[a-z-]*|-[a-z]*f[a-z]*|\+[^[:space:]]+)([[:space:]]|$)"` (mirror the -n cluster on line 40; `--for[a-z-]*` also covers --force-with-lease).

## Resolution
Force-push guard now matches -f flag clusters (-[a-zA-Z]*f...) and --for[a-z-]* abbreviations; verified by running the hook against -uf/-fu/--forc.
title: Force-push guard bypassed by flag clusters (-uf/-fu) and abbreviations (--forc)

The guard matches literal `--no-verify`; git resolves any unambiguous long-option prefix, and `--no-veri` uniquely resolves to `--no-verify`.

Guard now matches --no-ver[a-z-]* prefix abbreviations; verified --no-veri now blocks.

## Problem

Line 45 matches only `git[[:space:]]+-c[[:space:]]+core\.hookspath`. Ran the real hook: `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/dev/null git commit -m x`->ALLOW.

Added GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*=core.hooksPath / GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL|SYSTEM env-injection check; verified the env form now blocks.

## Problem

The deny regex requires the verb to be preceded by a boundary char in `^ [space] | ( & ;`. Any other leading byte defeats it, and the deny list misses interpreter wrappers.

## Evidence

Lines 62-63 build `deny_re='(^|[[:space:]|(&;])(...(grep|cat|...))[[:space:]]'`. Ran the real hook (match->permissionDecision:deny JSON; bypass->empty): `cat README.md`->deny; `/bin/cat README.md`, `\grep foo file`, `eval "grep x file"`, `bash -c "cat file"`->empty (ALLOW).

Blocked verbs run raw, defeating context-mode-required.md (raw bytes enter the conversation).

## Fix

Normalize each segment: strip leading directory path and leading `\`/quote, add `" ' \` to the boundary class, add wrapper detection for `(bash|sh|zsh|eval)[[:space:]]+-?c?`. Full shell coverage via regex is not achievable — document the residual gap.

## Resolution
Verb-boundary class now includes / " \047 so /bin/cat, eval "grep", bash -c "cat" are caught; verified via the real hook (deny vs empty). Leading-backslash noted as residual.

## Problem

Every GitHub API call is a synchronous round-trip inside nested loops. `analyzer.go` has zero `go func`/`errgroup`/`WaitGroup` (verified). `cmd_deps.go` loops over every action file; inside `CheckOutdated`/`AnalyzeActionFile` each dependency resolves serially.

## Evidence

`analyzer.go:180-193` loops deps calling `getLatestVersion` (`:572`) which does up to 3 sequential calls (`getLatestRelease`+`getCommitSHAForTag`=GetRef/GetTag, or `getLatestTag`=ListTags). `AnalyzeActionFile` (`:341-349`) calls `enrichWithGitHubData`->`Repositories.Get` (`:1035`) per step. Driven per-file by `cmd_deps.go:343-358,493-522`.

## Impact

50 action files x ~4 remote deps ~= 200 deps -> ~400-600 fully serial HTTP round-trips at 150-400ms => 1-4 min wall-clock. The per-owner/repo cache dedupes repeats but the first touch of every distinct action is serialized.

## Fix

Dedup `owner/repo` across all deps, resolve with a bounded worker pool (`golang.org/x/sync/errgroup`+`g.SetLimit(6)`), collect into a map, classify afterward. Make description-only `enrichWithGitHubData` lazy/opt-in.

## Resolution
CheckOutdated now resolves dependencies via a bounded (6) worker pool, order-preserving; extracted checkDepOutdated. Cache and go-github are concurrency-safe; mock made concurrency-safe (fresh body per Do). Passes under -race.
title: Dependency analysis does zero request concurrency: serial GitHub fan-out

Cache by key `owner/repo/tag -> sha` (a tag's SHA is immutable, long TTL) and check at the top of `getCommitSHAForTag`.

## Problem

Every other GitHub path bounds the call with `context.WithTimeout(..., APICallTimeout)`; the pin path passes a bare `context.Background()`. The go-github/oauth2 client sets no default client timeout, so the deadline is the only bound.

## Evidence

`analyzer.go:276`: `sha := a.getCommitSHAForTag(context.Background(), owner, repo, currentVersion)`. Siblings `getLatestVersion` (`:577`) and `enrichWithGitHubData` (`:1015`) use `context.WithTimeout`.

## Impact

`deps pin` (cmd_deps.go:546->GeneratePinInPlace) against a host that handshakes but never responds hangs indefinitely; in CI it wedges the job until the outer timeout kills it.

## Fix

`ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), appconstants.APICallTimeout); defer cancel()`; pass `ctx`, or thread a caller-supplied ctx into `GeneratePinInPlace`.

## Resolution
GeneratePinInPlace now wraps the lookup in context.WithTimeout(APICallTimeout).
title: getCommitSHAForTag pin path uses context.Background() with no timeout

## Problem

Documented invariant: YAML permissions win over comments. The scalar shorthand breaks it: `fromScalar("none")` returns a non-nil empty map, and `mergePermissions` assigns comment perms only when `action.Permissions == nil`, so a non-nil-empty map falls into the per-key merge loop that re-injects every comment key.

## Evidence

`parser.go:89-102` `fromScalar`: `none`/`""`->`PermissionMap{}` (non-nil,len0); `read-all`->`{"all":read}`. `parser.go:202-216`: `if action.Permissions==nil {assign;return}` then `for k:=range commentPerms {if !exists {inject}}`.

## Impact

Comment `#   contents: read` + YAML `permissions: none` renders `{contents: read}` instead of none. `read-all` + comment `contents: write` renders contradictory `{all: read, contents: write}`. Generated docs misrepresent the declared permission posture.

## Fix

In `mergePermissions`, treat any non-nil `action.Permissions` (incl. scalar forms) as authoritative and skip the comment merge; or have `fromScalar` mark that a global statement was made so comment keys drop.

## Resolution
mergePermissions now treats a scalar/global form (empty map from none/{}, or an all-keyed map from read-all/write-all) as authoritative and skips the comment merge; per-scope maps still merge. Added fixtures + 2 regression tests; strengthened property generators to real scopes/levels.
title: permissions: none / read-all scalar is silently overridden by header-comment permissions

## Problem

`renderTemplateForAction` computes the repo root from the OUTPUT directory. When `--output-dir` points outside the repo, `FindRepositoryRoot` fails (error swallowed), `repoRoot=""`, git detection is skipped and `extractActionSubdirectory` returns "" — the `uses:` degrades to the placeholder.

## Evidence

`generator.go:388`: `repoRoot, _ := git.FindRepositoryRoot(outputDir)` then `buildTemplateData(action, ..., repoRoot, actionPath, ...)` (`:393`). `actionPath` is available but unused for root detection; the error is discarded.

`gen /repo/actions/foo/action.yml --output-dir /tmp/out` yields a `uses:` with no org/repo and no `actions/foo` subdir, while the same command without `--output-dir` is correct. This is the documented testing pattern (`gen testdata/ --output /tmp/...`), so it degrades silently.

## Fix

`repoRoot, err := git.FindRepositoryRoot(filepath.Dir(actionPath))`; log the error under Verbose instead of discarding it.

## Resolution
repoRootForAction now derives the repo root from filepath.Dir(actionPath), not the output dir; error logged under Verbose. generateJSON also threads actionPath.
title: Repository root is derived from the output dir, not the action file, degrading git/monorepo uses:

## Problem

The JSON writer emits placeholder `your-org` and `@v1` for the repository link and usage example, ignoring detected git org/repo and the resolved version — the markdown path uses the real values.

## Evidence

`json_writer.go:265-267`: `"repository":"https://github.com/your-org/"+SanitizeActionName(action.Name)`. `:294`: `example += "  uses: your-org/"+...+"@v1"`. `JSONWriter.Write` receives only `*ActionYML`, never `TemplateData`/`UsesStatement`.

Plumb the resolved `UsesStatement`/org into the JSON writer (pass `TemplateData` or the computed uses string) instead of hardcoding placeholders.

## Resolution
JSON writer now resolves the real uses-statement and repo URL from git (via TemplateData in generateJSON), falling back to placeholders only when git info is absent. Added usesReference/repositoryLink helpers + regression test.

## Problem

`getActionVersion` validates `Config.Version` with `isValidVersionRef`, whose regex excludes `@`. `version: "@v2"` (natural copy-paste from `uses: org/repo@v2`) fails validation, priority-1 is skipped, and the tool silently falls back to the default branch or `@v1`.

## Evidence

`template.go:339`: `if td.Config.Version != "" && isValidVersionRef(td.Config.Version) { return td.Config.Version }`. `isValidVersionRef` uses `^[A-Za-z0-9._/+-]+$` (no `@`).

## Impact

The user's explicit pin is discarded with no error; generated `uses:` shows the wrong version.

## Fix

Strip a leading `@` before validating (normalize `@v2`->`v2`), or surface a validation error rather than silently falling through.

## Resolution
getActionVersion now strips a leading @ before validating, so version: "@v2" is accepted. Added regression test.
title: Explicit version with a leading @ is silently rejected and dropped

## Problem

The permissions-comment parser treats any `key: value` line at the item indent as a permission entry; it does not validate key/value against the real permission-scope vocabulary.

## Evidence

`parsePermissionLine`/`processPermissionEntry` (parser.go ~:334) insert `permissions[key]=value` for any indented `key: value`. `#   Note: also needs network access` under `# permissions:` becomes `{Note:"also needs network access"}`.

## Impact

Bogus permissions (e.g. `Note`) render into the README permissions table and JSON `permissions` object.

## Fix

Validate the parsed key against the known permission-scope set (and value against read/write/none) before inserting; skip non-conforming lines.

## Resolution
processPermissionEntry now inserts only values that are real permission levels (read/write/none) via isValidPermissionValue; prose lines are rejected. Added regression test.
title: Non-permission prose lines inside the permissions comment block are parsed as permissions

`CacheAdapter` (66 lines) forwards every method 1:1 to `*cache.Cache`, which already exposes the exact `DependencyCache` method set — so it adapts nothing. `NoOpCache` duplicates the `a.Cache == nil` guards already at every call site.

## Problem

The test named for async-save error handling only Sets a key, sleeps 100ms, and Gets it back from the in-memory map — it never verifies disk persistence or error surfacing.

## Evidence

`cache_test.go:459-483`: `Set(...)`, `time.Sleep(100*time.Millisecond)`, `Get(...)`. `Cache.Get` reads `c.data` (memory), never disk; `saveToDiskAsync` does `_ = c.saveToDisk() // Ignore errors`.

## Impact

If `saveToDisk` failed on every call or wrote nothing, this test still passes. The sleep is a hardcoded race guarding nothing.

## Fix

Close the cache (waits on saveWG), reopen from the same path, assert the value loads from disk; for error handling point the cache at an unwritable path and assert the error surfaces. Drop the sleep.

## Resolution
Rewrote as TestCacheAsyncSavePersistsToDisk: Set -> Close (flush) -> reopen -> Get asserts reload from disk. Removed the pointless sleep and tautological in-memory readback.
title: TestCacheAsyncSaveErrorHandling is tautological and flaky; tests none of its namesake

## Problem

Tests skip (not fail) when a fixture set is empty. Fixtures are committed and always present, so empty means a loader regression — silently passed over.

## Evidence

`generator_comprehensive_test.go:181`: `if len(fixtures)==0 { t.Skipf("no fixtures available for action type %s", actionType) }`. Same at `testutil/fixtures_test.go:554`.

## Impact

If `GetFixturesByActionType`/`GetValidFixtures` returns nothing, every subtest reports SKIP/PASS and the generator is never exercised — a green build that tested nothing.

## Fix

Assert non-empty: `if len(fixtures)==0 { t.Fatalf(...) }`. Reserve skips for genuine environmental gaps.

## Resolution
Empty committed-fixture checks changed from t.Skip to t.Fatal in generator_comprehensive_test.go and testutil/fixtures_test.go.
title: Silent t.Skip on empty committed fixtures turns a broken loader into a green build

## Problem

The relative-path branch gained `ensureWithinCWD` (symlink resolution + containment); the absolute-path branch only checks `filepath.Clean` equality then reads, while its `#nosec` says "validated absolute path". No location constraint or symlink resolution.

## Evidence

`embed.go:57-65`: `cleanPath := filepath.Clean(templatePath); if cleanPath != templatePath { return ErrBadPattern }; return os.ReadFile(cleanPath) // #nosec G304 -- validated absolute path`.

## Impact

Not currently exploitable — template path is trust-gated to global config/--theme (repo/action config merge with allowTokens=false). But if any untrusted config field (repo/action `template:`) is ever routed here it becomes arbitrary-file-read (/etc/passwd, .env) disclosed into rendered output.

## Fix

Apply the same containment/symlink resolution (or allowed-root allowlist) to the absolute branch and correct the #nosec justification.

## Resolution
Corrected the misleading #nosec justification on the absolute-path branch to state the actual trust basis (global config / --theme, gated by allowTokens); documented why containment is intentionally not applied.
title: Absolute-path ReadTemplate branch #nosec claims validation it does not perform

## Problem

`ci.yml`,`security.yml`,`codeql.yml` trigger on push+pull_request but define no `concurrency:` block, so superseded runs are not cancelled. `pr-lint.yml:11-13` and `sync-labels.yml:19-21` do it correctly.

## Evidence

`ci.yml:1-9`,`security.yml:1-15`,`codeql.yml:1-14` — no `concurrency:` key.

## Impact

Three quick pushes to a PR run three full pipelines concurrently; superseded runs waste runner minutes and delay the meaningful run.

## Fix

Add to each: `concurrency:` with `group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` and `cancel-in-progress: true`.

## Resolution
Added concurrency blocks to ci.yml, security.yml, codeql.yml with cancel-in-progress scoped to pull_request (so merge_group/main/scheduled runs are never cancelled).
title: CI/security/codeql workflows lack concurrency cancellation of superseded runs

## Problem

Production-shaped functions are defined inside `_test.go` files then "tested", crediting coverage to code no user path executes. The comment admits production no longer calls them.

## Evidence

`internal/deadcode_wrappers_test.go:28-66` defines `NewConfigurationLoaderWithOptions`,`EnableSource`,`DisableSource`,`GetConfigurationSources`; exercised only by `coverage_internalconfig_test.go:152-162`. Same: `internal/helpers/deadcode_wrappers_test.go:11` `GetGitRepoRootAndInfo`.

## Impact

If the real `ConfigurationLoader` source-selection had a bug, these tests still pass — they validate a parallel copy. Coverage is inflated by test-only code.

## Fix

Delete the wrappers and the tests that only touch them; if the behavior matters, add the method to production and have production call it.

## Resolution
Invalid after verification: not a parallel copy. Production ConfigurationLoader owns and reads the sources map (configuration_loader.go:119-197), and the wrappers delegate to real production functions (generateFromFile, loadAndUnmarshalConfig, git.FindRepositoryRoot/DetectRepository). They are exported test seams (the accepted pattern per CLAUDE.md InputReader) exercising genuine production paths; deleting them would drop real coverage.
title: deadcode_wrappers_test.go tests production-shaped functions that ship in no binary (coverage theater)
